name: Aperture Finance arbitrary call approval drain

classification.summary: The closed-source Aperture router forwarded caller-supplied call targets and calldata without validation, letting the attacker make the contract invoke ERC-20 transferFrom() and ERC-721 transfers against the standing token and Uniswap V3 position approvals users had granted it.

loss.notes: BlockSec reports approximately $3.67 million of gross assets lost across the Aperture campaign on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Base. The structured asset component is the exact WBTC amount transferred from a victim in the selected Ethereum transaction; it is only one component of the reported cross-chain total. No recovery is netted from the exploit-time loss.

lastCodeChange.description: The vulnerable arbitrary-call path is part of the target's immutable direct runtime, created by the factory in this transaction and unchanged through the exploit.

sources.note: Reviewed the live Ethereum transaction, receipt, call trace, factory creation transaction, pre-exploit runtime and hash, runtime control flow, and BlockSec's campaign analysis. The selected transaction calls selector 0x67b34120 on 0xd83d960debec397fb149b51f8f37dd3b5cfa8913; its user-controlled target and calldata make that contract call WBTC.transferFrom(victim, attacker, 36.91885364 WBTC) against a standing approval. The target is a direct contract with no delegatecall path in its runtime. It was created internally by factory 0x13b0d85ccb8bf860b6b79af3029fca081ae9bef2 in transaction 0x239acc3db4cf951a671fab224129ba26250d96d3dce6ea0d934eee8d26b7c9f7 at 24020090:222; 0xbeef63ae5a2102506e8a352a5bb32aa8b30b3112 is the transaction sender, not the target's creatorAddress. The pre-exploit runtime hash matches the declared artifact and the deployment is its last code change. BlockSec reports approximately $3.67 million lost across the same arbitrary-call campaign on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Base.

limitations: The cross-chain $3.67 million campaign total is retained from BlockSec reporting; only the selected Ethereum transaction's WBTC component was independently quantified here.
